en.summary: Rob Savage's new horror film, based on Josh Malerman's novel, has dropped its first trailer, featuring a terrifying jump scare and a disturbing question. Jessica Chastain stars as a mother whose doppelganger seeks entry into her daughter's heart.
en.body:
The first trailer for **Rob Savage**'s upcoming horror film, **Other Mommy**, has arrived, and it’s already making waves with a jump scare that’s proving remarkably effective. Set to release on May 8, 2026, the film stars **Jessica Chastain** and is based on **Josh Malerman**'s novel *Incidents Around the House*. The trailer offers a glimpse into a darkening world where a young girl named Bela forms a disturbing relationship with an entity that looks exactly like her mother.

The brief description accompanying the trailer hints at the core terror: **Other Mommy** is "a terrifying trip into the darkening world of a young girl, Bela, who forms a relationship with a sinister entity in her home who looks uncannily like her own mother." This premise echoes the unsettling vibe of **Henry Selick**'s *Coraline*, though **Other Mommy** is decidedly not for children. The source material, Malerman's novel, delves deeper into the psychological dread, presenting a chilling scenario where an entity, "Other Mommy," relentlessly asks eight-year-old Bela, “Can I go inside your heart?” As incidents around the house escalate, it becomes clear that Other Mommy is growing impatient, and Bela’s family is at risk if she doesn’t comply.

The trailer itself has generated significant buzz, particularly for its well-timed scare that has caught many viewers off guard. Social media reactions indicate a mix of trepidation and excitement, with many users sharing their startled responses. The connection to **Coraline** is often made, but the tone of **Other Mommy** appears to lean into a much darker, more mature form of horror, focusing on familial breakdown and invasive psychological threats. The film, produced by Blumhouse and **James Wan**'s Atomic Monster, promises a chilling exploration of a child’s perception versus a sinister reality.

## A Sinister Question and a Familiar Face

The trailer’s most potent element, beyond the jump scare, is the insidious question posed by the titular entity: "Can I go inside your heart?" This simple yet deeply unnerving inquiry forms the emotional and narrative core of the film. **Jessica Chastain**'s presence as the mother figure, potentially both the real one and the horrifying doppelganger, adds a layer of gravitas to the unfolding nightmare. Her performance will be crucial in navigating the complex psychological landscape of the story. The adaptation by **Succession** writer **Nathan Elston** suggests a nuanced approach to the source material, aiming to translate Malerman's atmospheric dread into a compelling cinematic experience.

## What Fans Are Saying

Online discussions, particularly on platforms like TikTok, show a community buzzing with anticipation and a touch of playful fear. The trailer’s jump scare has become a talking point, with many sharing their own startled reactions and predicting the film's impact. Fans of **Josh Malerman**'s novel are eager to see how **Rob Savage**, known for his atmospheric horror like *Host* and *Dashcam*, will bring the unsettling narrative to life. The blend of a familiar, domestic setting with a terrifying supernatural presence, embodied by a mother figure, taps into primal fears, making **Other Mommy** a highly anticipated entry in the horror genre for 2026.

## What's Next

**Other Mommy** is slated for release on May 8, 2026. With the trailer now out, audiences can anticipate further promotional material and potentially a deeper dive into the film's terrifying premise as the release date approaches.

By Molly Templeton | Published on July 21, 2026 Screenshot: Universal Pictures Comment 0 Share New Share Other Mommy Trailer Contains a Sneakily Effective Jump Scare&url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Other Mommy Trailer Contains a Sneakily Effective Jump Scare” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Screenshot: Universal Pictures It’s called Other Mommy , not Other Mother , but you’d be forgiven for making a connection between Rob Savage’s new horror film and Henry Selick’s Coraline adaptation. Both have creepy moms who are … other . But Coraline is for kids, and Other Mommy most certainly is not. The film is based on Josh Malerman’s novel Incidents Around the House , adapted by Succession writer Nathan Elston. The trailer comes with only the briefest of descriptions: Other Mommy is “a terrifying trip into the darkening world of a young girl, Bela, who forms a relationship with a sinister entity in her home who looks uncannily like her own mother.” The book synopsis gives a better sense of the unnerving vibe here: To eight-year-old Bela, her family is her world. There’s Mommy, Daddo, and Grandma Ruth. But there is also Other Mommy, a malevolent entity who asks her every day: “Can I go inside your heart?” When horrifying incidents around the house signal that Other Mommy is growing tired of asking Bela the question over and over, Bela understands that unless she says yes, her family will soon pay. Other Mommy is getting restless, stronger, bolder. Only the bonds of family can keep Bela safe, but other incidents show cracks in her parents’ marriage. The safety Bela relies on is about to unravel. But Other Mommy needs an answer. Jessica Chastain plays both real mom and alarming mom, who is not good at cooking, but very good at … contortion? There’s a jump scare at about 1:15 in the trailer, below, for which I was deeply unprepared. Chastain is joined by Jay Duplass ( Somebody Somewhere ) as “Daddo” and Arabella Olivia Clark as Bela. The cast also includes the perpetually under-appreciated Dichen Lachman ( Severance ), Arian Moayed ( Succession ) and Karen Allen ( Raiders of the Lost Ark ). Director Savage is known for Host and The Boogeyman ; this is not his first time absolutely freaking audiences out. Other Mommy is in theaters October 9.[end-mark] The post The Other Mommy Trailer Contains a Sneakily Effective Jump Scare appeared first on Reactor .
